headline: 10 cases of genocide and killings: Extradition process begins for former IGP Benazir
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal prosecution has initiated legal and diplomatic steps via Interpol to bring back the former police chief from Dubai.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal prosecution has revealed that at least 10 cases involving genocide, killings, and enforced disappearances are being investigated against former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed.
Benazir, who is currently under arrest in Dubai, is alleged to have been directly involved in numerous crimes during his tenure as both the RAB chief and the IGP.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam identified Benazir as one of the 'key actors' in the Shapla Chattar incident and stated he was directly involved in the Ekram Commissioner murder case in Chattogram.
The state has already begun legal and diplomatic procedures through the National Central Bureau (NCB) and Interpol to extradite him to Bangladesh.
Warrant copies have been sent to the police's special branch and the NCB to facilitate the issuance of red notices or other color-coded notices via Interpol.
The prosecution believes that the evidence in these cases shows a clear connection to Benazir, with investigations into several of the cases now in their final stages.
caption:
Former IGP Benazir Ahmed faces 10 cases of genocide and killings. The process to bring him back from Dubai has officially begun.

The International Crimes Tribunal prosecution has revealed that at least 10 cases involving genocide, killings, and enforced disappearances are being investigated against former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed.

Benazir, who is currently under arrest in Dubai, is alleged to have been directly involved in numerous crimes during his tenure as both the RAB chief and the IGP.

Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam identified Benazir as one of the 'key actors' in the Shapla Chattar incident and stated he was directly involved in the Ekram Commissioner murder case in Chattogram.

The state has already begun legal and diplomatic procedures through the National Central Bureau (NCB) and Interpol to extradite him to Bangladesh.

Warrant copies have been sent to the police's special branch and the NCB to facilitate the issuance of red notices or other color-coded notices via Interpol.

The prosecution believes that the evidence in these cases shows a clear connection to Benazir, with investigations into several of the cases now in their final stages.

headline_marked: Ad-Din Hospital [[denies bribery attempts]] after license revocation
headline: Ad-Din Hospital denies bribery attempts after license revocation
summary: Executive Director Dr. Sheikh Mohiuddin challenges the Health Minister to prove allegations that the hospital tried to bribe him to save its license.
details: Following the revocation of its license due to the death of six newborns, Ad-Din Hospital's Executive Director Dr. Sheikh Mohiuddin has denied allegations of attempting to bribe the Health Minister.
Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain recently claimed that the hospital tried to offer him millions of taka to save its license, but he refused the bribes.
At a press conference in Moghbazar, Dr. Mohiuddin challenged the minister to provide proof of the bribery allegations, stating he had no reason to offer such money.
The hospital authority expressed respect for the government's decision to cancel the license, viewing it as a lesson for other private medical colleges.
They are currently working to fix deficiencies identified in a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) inspection report and plan to appeal the decision within 30 days.

Regarding the newborn deaths, the director stated that the exact cause is still unknown and called for a state-level forensic investigation, noting concerns over ventilation and carbon dioxide levels.
The hospital has stopped admitting new patients, though critical patients in the ICU and NICU are being managed as immediate transfer would be risky.
A bakery located on the upper floor of the hospital building has also been closed following government objections.
caption:
Did Ad-Din Hospital try to bribe the Health Minister to save its license? The hospital's director says 'no' and challenges the minister to prove it.

Following the revocation of its license due to the death of six newborns, Ad-Din Hospital's Executive Director Dr. Sheikh Mohiuddin has denied allegations of attempting to bribe the Health Minister.

Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain recently claimed that the hospital tried to offer him millions of taka to save its license, but he refused the bribes.

At a press conference in Moghbazar, Dr. Mohiuddin challenged the minister to provide proof of the bribery allegations, stating he had no reason to offer such money.

The hospital authority expressed respect for the government's decision to cancel the license, viewing it as a lesson for other private medical colleges.

They are currently working to fix deficiencies identified in a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) inspection report and plan to appeal the decision within 30 days.

Regarding the newborn deaths, the director stated that the exact cause is still unknown and called for a state-level forensic investigation, noting concerns over ventilation and carbon dioxide levels.

The hospital has stopped admitting new patients, though critical patients in the ICU and NICU are being managed as immediate transfer would be risky.

A bakery located on the upper floor of the hospital building has also been closed following government objections.

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, bdnews24.com, Somoy News
